subject: Data Engineering
title: Lake Storage Architecture
description: A quick, practical guide to Lake Storage Architecture.

hook.text: A well-organized lake has layers: raw, cleaned, and curated. A disorganized lake has one folder called 'data'.

buildup.text: The raw layer stores data exactly as received from sources. No changes, no cleaning — a faithful copy.

discovery.text: The cleaned layer applies validation, deduplication, and standardization. The curated layer serves business queries.

twist.text: Skipping the raw layer means losing the ability to reprocess data when transformation logic changes.

climax.text: Three layers — raw, cleaned, curated — give you immutability at the bottom and usability at the top.

punchline.text: Raw at the bottom. Curated at the top. Layers matter.

quiz.question: Why should a data lake always keep a raw layer?
options: To reprocess data when transformation logic changes
Because raw data is smaller than cleaned data
